chunks.arabic_text: عَنْ رَجُلٍ زَارَعَ مُسْلِمًا أَوْ مُعَاهَدًا فَأَنْفَقَ فِيهِ نَفَقَةً ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُ فِي بَيْعِهِ أَلَهُ ذَلِكَ

translations.en: About a man who entered into a farming arrangement with a Muslim or a Mu'ahid, then spent some expense on it, and afterward it occurred to him to sell it—does he have that right?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ يَشْتَرِيهِ بِالْوَرِقِ فَإِنَّ أَصْلَهُ طَعَامٌ.

translations.en: He said: "He may buy it with silver, for its origin is food."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sale of an agricultural interest after expenses have been invested in it. The Imam عليه السلام permits the transaction in silver, noting that the underlying subject of the arrangement is food produce.
en.seo_question: Can a person sell an agricultural partnership interest for silver after spending on it?

key_terms.زَارَعَ: entered into a farming or cultivation arrangement
key_terms.مُعَاهَدًا: a non-Muslim under covenant or protected agreement
key_terms.بِالْوَرِقِ: with silver coins or silver currency
key_terms.طَعَامٌ: food produce, the underlying commodity in context
